name: Huitoto, Nüpode
catalog_quote: Por regla general el acento de intensidad recae en la primera silaba de la palabra [in general an intensity accent is located on the first syllable of the word]. (Minor & Hendrich de Minor 1971:137) [...] There are many exceptions. Stress is accompanied by high pitch. (Minor 1956:137)

audit.recode_to: Not fixed-strict. Recode to initial-default with lexically specified (phonemic) stress — i.e. strict=false, kind = the catalog's lexical/unpredictable-with-initial-default class (e.g. 'fixed-lax'/'lexical' per taxonomy), citing Minor 1956:137 ('complex suprasegmental phoneme of stress accompanied by high pitch') as deciding source and Minor & Minor 1971:137 as the orthographic default; note Wojtylak 2017:5 fn.2 ('only Murui and Mɨka have fixed accent position (word-initial). Mɨnɨka and Nɨpode appear to have different patterns of accent placement').
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim on the page image of the held 1971/2008 vocabulario, p.137. (2) But the coding 'fixed-strict initial' over-reads an orthographic convention: the same sentence says non-initial stress exists and is written with an accent, the same page prints jopóchupbi, atdáva, muìnánɨ, and sampled dictionary pages (pp.20, 30) show accent-marked non-initial stress on roughly half the polysyllabic headwords. (3) The primary phonology of this very dialect, Minor 1956 (fetched sources now, open, page image read), sets up stress+high pitch as a suprasegmental PHONEME and states no positional rule; its transcribed forms carry stress on varying syllables. StressTyp2's own passage already flagged 'many exceptions'. (4) Wojtylak 2017 (held), the current authority on Witoto, states that only Murui and Mɨka have fixed word-initial accent and that Nɨpode's accent placement differs. (5) No better
audit.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: re-verified on the page image of the held file, book p.137 = PDF p.147 (Apéndice II 'Pronunciación y ortografía'): 'Por regla general el acento de intensidad recae en la primera sílaba de la palabra. Cuando no es así, se marca sobre la sílaba acentuada.' — verbatim; same page prints jopóchupbi 'casita', atdáva 'gallina' with marked non-initial stress. The second half of the record's dq ('There are many exceptions. Stress is accompanied by high pitch. (Minor 1956:137)') is a StressTyp2 compiler gloss: the fetched sources IJAL scan

sources.quote: As a general rule the stress (intensity accent) falls on the first syllable of the word. When that is not the case, it is written over the stressed syllable.

sources.citation: Minor, Eugene E. 1956. Witoto vowel clusters. International Journal of American Linguistics 22(2): 131-137. doi:10.1086/464357 (Muinánɨ dialect, Ampiyacu River, Peru, fieldwork 1952-54).
sources.quote: 'The six vowel phonemes are i, e, a, o, u, ɨ. There is a complex suprasegmental phoneme of stress accompanied by high pitch.' Stress is treated as phonemic (contrastive); no positional rule is given anywhere in the article; cited forms show stress on the first syllable (hópo 'house', héiaɨ 'many rats', tékuai 'jump', áɨjue 'large') and on later syllables (uaiʔɨ́dɨkue 'I'm staying', daɨiñédikaɨ 'not like we are', makáoiakade p.131).
sources.note: The only phonological analysis of Nɨpode (same author, same Ampiyacu speakers as the 1971 vocabulario); it posits a stress PHONEME and gives no initial rule, so it should replace the orthography note as deciding source. fetched sources now (open archive.org microfilm scan).

sources.citation: Jiménez, Myriam. 2013. Exploración fonética, acústico-articulatoria, de las vocales del uitoto, dialecto nɨpode. Trabajo de grado (pregrado), Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Bogotá. 48 pp. (repositorio.unal.edu.co handle unal/52940)
sources.quote: No statement on word stress or accent placement; instrumental study of vowel formants, duration, F0 and intensity at vowel midpoints only. §1.4 confirms prior Nɨpode-specific work is limited to Minor 1956, Minor & Minor and Griffiths (2000/2001, unpublished lexicon).
sources.locator: full text searched (acento/acentua/sílaba/tono/prosod/intensidad); §1.4 pp.3-4 literature review
sources.note: Only instrumental work on Nɨpode (Glottolog hhtype phonology); fetched sources now — silent on stress, so it closes the question of whether an acoustic stress study exists (it does not).
